completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed three failure modes in the online-discovery -> Zotero+PDF -> ingest bridge: (a) arXiv-only records now pass a synthesized 10.48550/arXiv.<id> DOI to bypass zot add --pdf's hard-fail; (b) staging-PDF and sources/<doc_id>/ orphan leaks are cleaned up on all forced-failure paths (including a fifth continue branch added concurrently by an unrelated task, and a pre-existing set-e/pipefail bug that made one branch unreachable, both fixed); (c) ONLINE_INGEST_PIPELINE_FAILED rationales are enriched with a manual-only Class A/Class B diagnostic pointer. zotero-item-creation.md's understatement was corrected. All 7 plan phases completed and verified via a new 10-scenario forced-failure/stub harness; git diff confirmed no .claude/ path was touched.

memory_candidates.content: When testing a bash pipeline of scripts that resolve sibling tools via $SCRIPT_DIR/<name>.sh (rather than PATH), build a forced-failure harness by symlinking the real scripts under test into a task-local harness/bin/ directory alongside purpose-built stub executables for the siblings you want to control (same directory, so $SCRIPT_DIR-relative resolution picks up the stubs automatically). For network-calling siblings (curl, local HTTP APIs), prefer a stub that intercepts only the specific host/endpoint under test and passes every other call through to the real binary -- this lets real downloads still happen while controlling just the one lookup that needs to be deterministic (e.g. Unpaywall OA-location resolution).

Under `set -eo pipefail`, an assignment like `VAR=$(ls pattern 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xargs ...)` crashes the whole script with a bare, unexplained exit when the glob has no matches: the unmatched glob makes `ls` exit non-zero, pipefail propagates that through the rest of the pipeline into the assignment's own exit status, and `set -e` treats the assignment as a failed simple command. This silently makes any downstream `if [ -z "$VAR" ]` empty-check branch unreachable -- the intended graceful handling never runs. Guard with `VAR=$(...) || true` whenever a glob inside a piped command substitution might legitimately match nothing.
